newsitem.title: FRANCE: Now 5,000 French stations lack fuel, official says.
newsitem.headline: Now 5,000 French stations lack fuel, official says.

text.p: The number of French petrol stations hit by lack of fuel leaped to 5,000 on Thursday and most key depots were cut off as striking truckers continued to strangle deliveries, an industry ministry official said.
About 5,000 of France's 18,000 stations were either empty or feeling some kind of shortage on the 11th day of lorry blockades against oil depots and refineries, he said.
The same official had put the number of stations short of fuel at between 1,000 and 1,500 earlier on Thursday.
"It is getting worse," he told Reuters on Thursday evening after truckers spent the day tightening their blockades in icy weather despite government appeals to return to work.
Oil industry association UFIP said at least 2,500 stations were affected. But its estimates may not include the large number of supermarket stores which also sell petrol.
The industry ministry said 150 oil depots out of about 400 nationwide were blocked off behind barricades.
But these included two thirds of the most important large depots which supply the bulk of motorists' needs, he said.
Depots still untouched were mainly specialist places where various industrial fuels were stored.
The official said 52 departments, or counties, had now started requisitioning service stations to direct scarce fuel to users on a priority list. These include doctors and ambulances.
The number of areas were stations were being impounded had risen from 34 on Wednesday, the 10th day of the strike.
The official also gave a wider list of most critically affected regions.
These were the southeast, southwest and northwest -- already seen badly hit -- but also the central western parts of France and the northeastern region near Calais.
The capital Paris remained hardly affected.
